title: Israel and Iran agree to a ceasefire ending the twelve-day war
body:
On 23 June 2025, hours after Iran fired missiles at the Al Udeid air base in Qatar, US President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social a "complete and total" ceasefire between Israel and Iran. He set a timetable in which Iran would begin the ceasefire at 04:00 GMT on Tuesday 24 June and Israel would follow at 16:00 GMT, and he called it the end of the "Twelve Day War." On 24 June he wrote that the ceasefire was now in effect and asked that it not be violated. Qatar, at the request of the United States, contacted Iran to help broker the truce.

Netanyahu's office said he accepted the ceasefire and that Israel had achieved all its objectives. Iran's Supreme National Security Council said it agreed to the truce but did not trust Israel and had its hands on the trigger. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian announced the end of the war imposed on Iran by Israel.

The ceasefire had a rocky start. Israel accused Iran of violating the truce and ordered strikes on Tehran, and Iran rejected the accusation and denied launching missiles at Israel. Al Jazeera reported that an Iranian missile hit a building in Beersheba, killing at least four people. Another Al Jazeera report from 22 June had cited more than 400 deaths in Iran from Israeli attacks and at least 24 deaths in Israel from Iranian strikes. The ceasefire left the underlying nuclear dispute unresolved.
